headline: Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments report improved test-time selection across five domains
summary: Guan and Du introduce Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments (APT), a training-free method that generates candidate solutions and selects a winner through single-elimination matchups. In each matchup, multiple prompted verifiers compare the two candidates along distinct aspects and vote; position-swapped judgments are used to reduce order bias. The authors report that APT produced the best score in 14 of 15 generator-domain pairs across five tasks and three generators at eight candidates, outperforming self-consistency, reward-model selection and binary aspect approval in most comparisons. Their matched-budget and component ablations also favor the combination of pairwise comparison and aspect-specific voting. These are preprint-reported results, not independent replications. The evaluation does not cover coding or long-form writing, and the tournament can cost up to about four times the input tokens of binary multi-aspect approval and adds sequential latency.
